summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old male with a history of non-ischemic cardiomyopathy, atrial fibrillation, restrictive lung disease, type 2 diabetes, and recently treated lung cancer was admitted for a three-day history of worsening shortness of breath and orthopnea. Initial evaluation showed pulmonary edema on chest X-ray, elevated BNP, and mild renal impairment. His symptoms improved with diuresis, steroids, azithromycin, nebulizer treatments, and CPAP. Amiodarone was discontinued due to possible pulmonary toxicity. He was in sinus rhythm, and his INR rose to 3.1, prompting warfarin hold instructions. He was discharged home with improved respiratory status, continuing a short course of prednisone and azithromycin, new nicotine patch for smoking cessation, and home CPAP setup. Follow-up was arranged with pulmonology, oncology, and primary care.
